title: corporate reputation audit checklist
claim: Corporate reputation is tested long before a crisis hits, during routine supplier onboarding where compliance checks fail due to administrative drift.

evidence.detail: Observed across multi-year industrial supply chains where regulatory clearance slips due to unmonitored sub-tier partner compliance, eroding stakeholder trust before any public incident occurs.

reel_script.voiceover: Reputation dies in procurement long before any public crisis makes the front page.
reel_script.direction: Static shot of an industrial facility entrance with steady movement.

items.label: Vendor onboarding
items.detail: Cleared on price, missed on compliance

items.label: Audit gap
items.detail: Sub-tier risk left unmonitored for years

reel_script.voiceover: The vulnerability is rarely the flagship plant. It is the sub-contractor two tiers down who skipped an environmental clearance.

items.label: Checked publicly
items.detail: Core facilities and tier one partners

reel_script.voiceover: Effective corporate reputation management requires testing your supply chain before regulators do it for you.
Start by mapping every sub-contractor handling materials or waste inside your active project sites.
Never rely on a checked box in a portal. Request the physical, stamped permit from the local authority.
reel_script.direction: Close up of folders being updated.

reel_script.voiceover: Corporate reputation is not a communications output. It is an operational audit trail.

items.label: Communications
items.detail: Explains the past after the fact

caption:
Reputation dies in procurement.

In corporate reputation management, this is the decision that changes the outcome.

Most industrial firms spend weeks polishing annual sustainability reports while leaving sub-tier supplier onboarding to manual spreadsheets. When a regulatory breach happens two levels down, the press release does not save the contract.

Trust is structural, not rhetorical.

Send this to whoever oversees vendor compliance and risk this quarter.
